bio_structure: LIMITS: pages read with scrapling get/bulk_get. Berlin Biennale 13 artist pages (13.berlinbiennale.de) returned empty (JS-rendered). WebSearch budget ran out before kurimanzutto/Sadie Coles/Gagosian searches, so those were read by guessed URLs. Items marked [search snippet] were seen only in WebSearch result text, not on the page.

STRUCTURE A (biennial guide, ~40-110 words): header block with birth year, birth city, country; then 1-3 sentences of critical blurb in present tense, third person, surname repeated; then sometimes a signed credit with em dash (e.g. '—Eva Díaz'). Venice 2026 header example '1952, New Orleans, USA' https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2026/dawn-dedeaux ; '1961, Schoten, Belgium' https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2026/philip-aguirre-y-otegui ; '1970, Kano State, Nigeria' https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2026/marcia-kure

VENICE 2026 list format: bare '[year], [city], [country]' lines such as '1983, Manila, Philippines.' and '1946, Oxford, UK'; deceased participant 'Nancy Brooks Brody 1962-2023, New York, USA'; group line 'All live in New York City' https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2026/artists

VENICE 2026 residence format [search snippet]: 'Pio Abad was born in 1983 in Manila, Philippines and lives in London, UK'; 'Kader Attia was born in 1970 in Dugny, France and lives in Berlin, Germany and Paris, France' https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2026/artists

VENICE 2024 prize bios [search snippet]: '(London, UK, 1985, Lives in Hamburg, Germany and Lagos, Nigeria)' and '(Jerusalem, Palestine, 1936, Lives in New York City, USA)' i.e. order City, Country, Year, Lives in ... https://www.labiennale.org/en/news/biennale-arte-2024-stranieri-ovunque-foreigners-everywhere

'In the Central Pavilion, Aguirre presents ...' https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2026/philip-aguirre-y-otegui

VENICE blurb openers: 'In the work of Marcia Kure – spanning drawing, collage, pigment and assemblage – inscription functions as a structural event, rendering histories, ecologies and systems of value legible.' ; 'Social and political themes – particularly issues of migration and refugees – form the core of Philip Aguirre y Otegui's humanistic oeuvre.' ; 'The New Orleans-based artist Dawn DeDeaux has been grappling with its consequences...' Medium lists sit between en dashes. https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2026/marcia-kure
VENICE support line: 'With the additional support of [foundation]; [gallery], New York City; [gallery], Lagos' ends many artist pages https://www.labiennale.org/en/art/2026/marcia-kure

WHITNEY 2024 format: pronouns line '(he/him/they/them)'; 'Born 1978 in San Francisco, CA' / 'Lives in Los Angeles, CA' on two lines; medium label 'Film'; then one ~100-word paragraph about the work, not a CV. https://whitney.org/exhibitions/2024-biennial/art?section=26

WHITNEY paragraph pattern: '[Artist]'s film [Title] from 2023 offers an updated version of camp, providing an alternative to ... Influenced by science fiction, horror, and comedy—and conveying a surrealist sense of absurdity—Kantor's film suggests that ...' (work-first, no exhibitions list) https://whitney.org/exhibitions/2024-biennial/art?section=26

WHITNEY pairs and name-as-concept: 'Holly Herndon and Mat Dryhurst' share one entry; text 'This work by Holly Herndon and Mat Dryhurst is part of a project focused on training the data behind artificial intelligence (AI) models, opening new possibilities for its use.' https://whitney.org/exhibitions/2024-biennial/art?section=19 ; [search snippet] 'Holly Herndon (born 1980 in Johnson City, TN) and Mat Dryhurst (born 1984 in Birmingham, UK) live in Berlin, Germany' https://whitney.org/exhibitions/2024-biennial/art?section=19

RESIDENCE VARIANTS seen: 'lives and works in X'; 'lives and works between X and Y'; 'lives and works in Tokyo, Mexico City, New York and Paris'; 'Lives in X' (Whitney, Venice); 'based in Berlin'; 'New York-based artist'; 'Argentina-born, New York-based'; 'currently living and working in Barcelona'; 'where she continues to live and work'. (Whitney and Venice use 'Lives in'; Sharjah, Lisson, H&W, kurimanzutto use 'lives and works'.)

ORDER OF CV ELEMENTS in long gallery bios (H&W, Lisson, kurimanzutto, Sharjah): 1 practice sentence 2 themes/method 3 birth + education 4 solo exhibitions 5 group exhibitions/biennials 6 collections 7 awards/residencies 8 lives and works (sometimes last line: kurimanzutto, Sharjah). Short biennial/e-flux bios drop collections and keep: birth, lives/works, 3-6 solo shows, 3-6 group shows, one prize or education line.

LENGTH VARIANTS observed: Venice 2026 guide blurbs about 25-170 words; Whitney about 100 words of work description only; Sharjah about 110-160 words; e-flux museum bios about 65-190 words; gallery pages (Hauser & Wirth, Gagosian, kurimanzutto) 250-600 words with separate CV tabs. A 40-word biennial guide bio keeps: (b. year, city), lives in, medium list, one theme clause.

COLLECTIVES in surveyed pages: Venice 'a Palermo-based collective established in Paris in 2004 by the Italian–British artist duo ...' ; header 'Founded in ..., [year]'; Whitney lists 'Raqs Media Collective', 'Holly Herndon and Mat Dryhurst', 'People Who Stutter Create' as single entries; Frac Lorraine text 'the Immagine collective' ; e-flux Gwangju 2026 text lists participants by name only https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/6787431/16th-gwangju-biennaleyou-must-change-your-life

E-FLUX / GWANGJU 16 curatorial intro verbs [page text]: 'The Biennale unfolds as a journey across scales—from the molecular to the cosmic ...'; 'Artists approach change through multiple registers'; 'Moving audiences across scales and intensities, the exhibition approaches artistic practice as producing capacities to sense, endure, relate, imagine, and transform.' (list of 5 verbs) https://www.e-flux.com/announcements/6787431/16th-gwangju-biennaleyou-must-change-your-life

ABSENT FROM SAMPLE (do not use as 'seen'): 'Her practice spans', 'is an artist and researcher based in', 'works across sculpture, film and sound' were not found verbatim in the pages read. Closest verified forms: 'practice lies at the intersection of', 'works collaboratively across mediums in sound, performance, sculpture and video', 'is an artist, curator, and publisher', 'combines film, architectural installation, and sculpture'.

eflux_layout: Top block (article__top), left column, in order: bold artist name(s); bold-italic exhibition title; optional plain-text subtitle line (e.g. 'of what is just becoming reality', 'Smuggling as Resistance', 'Twenty Years in Focus'); date range 'October 3, 2026–January 31, 2027' (month name, day, year, en dash, no leading zeros); 'Add to Calendar' button.

Group shows or untitled-artist shows start with the bold-italic title only, with no artist line (Action Bodies, Family Album, Haunted, House of Day, House of Night). Multi-show announcements stack 'Artist: Title' pairs, then one date range (Swiss Institute, Frac Lorraine, Mosaic Rooms).

Event rows follow the dates, each as a bold label, colon, then date and time: 'Opening: October 2, 6–10pm' ; 'Opening at GAK Bremen: October 2, 7pm' ; 'Opening reception: September 4, 2–5pm, with curator and artists present' ; 'Artist talk: October 24, 2pm–3am, X in dialogue with Y' ; 'Workshop: October 16, 4pm' ; 'Curatorial tour: May 30, 5–6pm' ; 'Performance: June 2, 3–4:30pm'. Times use '6–8pm', '2pm–3am' (no zero padding, am/pm lowercase, en dash). Each row has its own 'Add to Calendar'. RSVP button appears when set.

Right column address block: bold venue name; street; city; postcode on its own line; country on its own line (e.g. 'Portikus / Alte Brücke 2 / Maininsel / Frankfurt am Main / 60594 / Germany'). Then 'Hours: Tuesday–Friday 12–7pm' with a second line for exceptions ('Thursday 11am–9pm'); then email/phone ('T +49 421 500897'), website link, and social links ('Instagram / Facebook').

Page header above the block: breadcrumb 'e-flux / Announcements'; H1 'Artist: *Title*' (artist, colon, italic title); H2 with the venue name linked to the e-flux directory; image carousel with captions in the form 'Artist, *Work*, 2025. Installation view, Venue. Photo: Name.'; announcement date line like 'October 1, 2026' (publication date, not show date).

Sidebar tags (hidden by default): 'Category' (e.g. Nature & Ecology) and 'Participants' (artist names as search links); Share (Email, Facebook, X, Copy Link); 'More from [Venue]' strip with older announcements below the text.

Body (article__body) is plain paragraphs with no headings; bold run-in labels for credits and sections: '**Artists:** ...', '**With:** ...', '**Curatorial team:**', '**Acknowledgements**', '**Catalogue**', '**Thanks to**', '**Events**', '**Biography**:'. Credits come last: 'Curated by ...', 'Director: ... / Curator: ... / Press contact: ...'.
The words 'Press release' were not used as a heading on any of the 28 pages read; the body simply starts with the release text. Institution boilerplate starts with 'About [Institution]' in bold.
Titles are written with italics for exhibition and work titles inside running text (*My Skeleton*, *Reflection of a Forest*) and with bold-italic in the top block.

Counts in the sample (n=28): 'Hours:' line present in 18; 'Opening:' style row present in 11; curator credit in 22; bio paragraph with '(b. year, city)' or '(city, year)' in 9; funder/support line in 10.

Multi-year programme announcements (not counted in the exhibition sample) exist on e-flux as 'Exhibition programme 2026' / 'Autumn 2026' / 'Programme 2025–26' with lists of 3-6 show titles and dates in one body.
